notes.title: Massive Improvements and QoL Patch is live!
notes.notes:
Hi everyone!

It's time for another fixes and tweaks patch (build 7874779)! We've added a bunch of QoL changes and fixes that'll make your time in the Sierra-verse smoother! ːclaineohohoː

Let's start with the 
[h2]Major fixes: [/h2]
[olist]
[*][b]Issue with pronouns and AU!Junius, UK spelling, and some minor typos plus punctuation.[/b] The majority of the week has been dedicated to trying to automate this process along with some punctuation issues and remaining UK spelling. All visual novel scenes, battle scenes, and overworld scenes should be problem free. We are still manually checking them during the directing process, but this is a great backup system to see if we missed anything. There are two victory lines that need to be re-recorded, but we'll slot them in as soon as we receive the lines.  If you see typoes we missed after the next patch, please let us know and we'll fix it ASAP! This also applies to all other issues with Junius selection like og!Junius appearing randomly during breaks. ːjeanthinkː

[*][b]Issue with retained settings and resolution changing.[/b] There was a bug that caused things like menu text and side quest text to overflow/display incorrectly when the resolution or fullscreen/windowed mode is changed. This should now be resolved. The game show also actively maintain your settings for both resolution and volume upon reboot without needing the menu to be accessed. 

[*][b]Background alignment bug on reload.[/b] Sometimes the background during visual novel sections would be misaligned when reloading a save twice. This should now be resolved.
[/olist]
[h2]Minor fixes:[/h2]
[list]
[*]There was a small issue with routing during the Strange Ships route that's now been fixed. 
[*]Fixed a minor bug that made it so you couldn't switch back to Sierra while in exoframe mode. 
[*]Improved stability.
[*]There was still an instance of Sierra's barrage ability being accessible before the main battle of Chapter 3. That's been resolved now, but still keep an eye out just in case! 
[*]Fixed an issue where small projectiles (like Lapis' guns and CIWS) disappear halfway to their target. 
[/list]
[h2]Next we have some quality of life changes!:[/h2]
[olist]
[*][b]Combat Reminder[/b] - In an effort to give players a bit more support, combat wise, we're including a mini reminder guide to the menu under a new "help" button. In the case you're confused or have forgotten what something did, pause at any point  to take a look! They will pop up automatically in some earlier missions so consider them a mini reminder tutorial. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9849113/5259cb8e76830e5f6da97599b0c3d202b3bd51d2.png[/img]

[*][b]Upgraded Textlog[/b] - The textlog has been upgraded! It will now record battle dialogue and retain lines until the max number of lines is reached or the game is rebooted. In addition, we also made it possible to access the log during battle cutscenes via the mouse scroll wheel or accessing the menu via ESC, pausing the action until the player exits the menu. This only applies when dialogue boxes are present so it shouldn't interfere during actual combat. ːallenshockː

[*][b]Opportunities[/b] - Opportunities are now specified to give hints on how to obtain them or tell players if it's inaccessible.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9849113/49725059ea823e002e6039acbae68e5ba6baea0b.png[/img]
[/olist]

[h3]Plus one minor QoL change: [/h3]
- Expanded on the Venus tutorial that explains turning off vector shields and allotting more EN has them regenerating faster.


We're still working on some big behind the scenes stuff so stay tuned! Thanks for supporting the game! ːaiheartː

notes.title: Sierra Ops Major Update is Finally Here!
notes.notes:
Heyo, Youko here! It's been a while since I've written the update, but I'm here to finally give you the full load down on our upcoming major update! We're still ironing out some bugs at the moment, but it'll be up soon! ːallenshockː

Here's our new adjusted trailer and opening ːaiheartː
[previewyoutube=9Jj2ATHK9AE;full][/previewyoutube]
[previewyoutube=IPc0x-K4A_g;full][/previewyoutube]

Just in case you missed our prior posts, this update will include: 
[olist]
[*] Female character option for the main character, Junius
[*] Story Mode difficulty 
[*] Arcade Mode 
[*] Voice Acted situational dialogue
[*] Misc (controller support, tutorials +, visual update)
[/olist]

Let's break down each of the above in more detail! ːashtonglareː

[h2]1. Female Junius [/h2]

For those of you who don't know, one of the ongoing memes in the Sierra Ops dev team is that [b]I, personally[/b] really want a female protagonist option and that Junius was always written to be more or less gender neutral so it'd be a relatively easy switch. Lo and behold, the pipedream is actually becoming a reality! ːallenshockː

Now, what does that actually mean in terms of contents?

As much as I'd like to give a Person 3 Portable experience, that's just not feasible for the size of our team and the scale of the game plus the resources we have on hand. As a result, the difference between the two protagonists will be relatively minor, but there will be a few instances of gender specific dialogue and scenes, but for all intent and purposes, feel free to pick whichever you like based on personal preferences. [b]This also applies to character routes/ romances[/b] (if you care about that sort of thing).

Since I know people are going to mod in gated off pairings anyway, we flat out decided to allow free access to all character routes for both protagonists to give everyone the best experience possible. Go and pursue your yuri and yaoi dreams (though it's technically shoujo and shonen ai)! I won't stop you! ːclaineohohoː

That said, if you're concerned about accidently romancing someone (I've had those nightmares in Mass Effect), don't worry. You have to explicitly pursue a romance to actually trigger it and the best friend route is always available if platonic relationships are more your jam. [b]Keep in mind, the romance aspect of the game was always on the lighter end and we are very PG-13[/b], so temper your expectations. :sweatyJess: 

[h2]2. Story mode [/h2]

Due to the nature of Sierra Ops being a hybrid visual novel/RTS/Shoot 'em up????? ːjeanthinkː, we've had a lot of complaints on both ends in regards to gameplay difficulty/ease/obtuseness and story length/ too much dialogue/ not enough gameplay. Story mode is our solution for those who just want to focus on story. 

Story mode is designed for those players who want to just experience the story and completely trivialize the gameplay. That said, because Sierra is a game that's impacted by gameplay performance, playing story mode will limit certain outcomes (most of them bad). We think this is a fair trade-off since the majority of players prefer to see good outcomes only, but at the end of the day, we're still gating off certain aspects of the story. It's definitely not an incomplete experience, but it's something to keep in mind. There's nothing wrong with practicing in story mode and then eventually moving to normal mode once you're more familiar with the gameplay.

That said, this doesn't mean that [b]all[/b] bad outcomes are barred from story mode. Story bad ends are still completely accessible! We hope that's enough to sate your story curiosity. 

[h2]3. Arcade Mode[/h2]

On the opposite end of the spectrum, we have Arcade mode! Arcade mode is for everyone who would prefer to completely skip the visual novel and dish it out on the battlefield instead! 

This mode features completely new stages, scenarios, and upgrades not available anywhere else in the game. It's completely uncoupled from the narrative of the game, so experiment to your heart's content with different load-outs, weapon configurations, etc. 

Even if you enjoy the narrative aspect of the game, this'll hopefully sate your appetite for new combat scenarios while we work on the next instalment of the story! 

We'll be updating this mode soon with new CAST and Lapis content at a later date so look forward to it!

[h2]4. Voice Acting [/h2]

As mentioned in earlier updates, we've been working to include some limited voice acting to the game. Due to the way scenes are structured and cost, we've largely limited voice acting to combat, victory, development port, side mission selection, and some other minor bits and bobs. Hopefully, this adds the little personal touches we're looking for so crew members actually feel like crew members!

You'll notice a new little pop-up in the bottom right corner of the screen that indicates who is talking and what they're saying if you ever get mixed up. A big thanks to all our voice actors who've devoted time to being in our game! 

We've tried to balance how much they play, so any feedback would be highly welcome. ːjeanthinkː

[h2]5. Pretty much everything else[/h2]

Along side the explanation heavy stuff above, here are a few more additions that'll be coming into your hands along with everything else!

[b]A. Controller support [/b]
It's exactly what's on the tin! As mentioned before, we've been looking into making Sierra controller compatible so you can play on the go with systems like steam deck and potentially in future console release (this is really far away). We're very interested in feedback, so please feel free to share it in our discord or the steam forums. Thank you ahead of time!

[b]B. Tutorials + [/b]
We've expended on the tutorials somewhat so certain mechanics and systems are better explained and have accompanying visuals. We hope this helps clear up whatever confusion there is, but let us know if it needs to be adjusted again! 

[b]C. Improved Visuals [/b]
Our amazing environment artist, Tobby, has given the battle graphics a total overhaul! Everything from weapons particle effects to backgrounds and ship damage states has been adjusted to be cleaner and more cohesive! Overall, everything has a cleaner and brighter look, and we're super thankful for his hard work!

He's also the one responsible for the new banners on Steam! Make sure to give him a round of applause if you like the changes! ːclaineohohoː
https://store.steampowered.com/app/364210/Sierra_Ops/

That's it from me! Thank you for supporting the game! ːaiheartː

notes.notes:
To everyone who's been waiting for a substantial update: We're really close to getting the major patch out. It should be ideally released on November 15th, and latest would be 20th. We're still waiting on two voice actors to submit their gameplay voiceovers, but if they don't make it, we'll push the voice acting forward and have their voices at a later date.
The patch will have the following:
1.  Female Junius option
2. Additional tutorials
3. Controller Support [b]*new*[/b]
4. Gameplay voices
5. Improved battle visuals [b]*new*[/b]
6. Arcade mode (alpha) [b]*new*[/b]
7. "Story" difficulty mode

For the second game, it's the same as last week - Youko has been writing Chapters 4 and 5 while also handling her dice business.
There's also a new background artwork by Tobby! It's the Hero's Monument located in Mondshire, Central Sector:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9849113/70e5aef12a03c375caef4505de08e3b75af10507.png[/img]

Lastly, on a more personal note: We apologize for pushing back the update schedule ːtiredadmiralː, we'll try to recover and go back to updating every Fridays once we have our irl stuff sorted out around January. Why January? Because that's the only time we can see if all our efforts in improving the game were worth it or not. We expect two upcoming major Steam Sale to happen, and if we still can't break past the bare minimum, we still have our last stand which is the 2nd game early access, but it'll be delayed the more we get negative income. 

We had a rough launch, 1.5 years of little to no support, and we've only started recovering recently. We try to stay positive that things will work out, that the game can stand on its own eventually. Once the major sales come out, we hope everyone can share Sierra Ops to their friends/colleagues so we can bring the rest of the story sooner to you. We promise that the journey in seeing Sierra to completion is worth it - after all, we aim to be one of the great sci-fi/mecha stories to be ever told.

notes.title: Weekly Update #14 - Rutherford VA decided, more WIPs!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone, Hel (Jason) here covering the update for this week!

As the title says, after a few hours of listening to 176 submissions and a tiebreaker between 3 participants, the team has decided to cast [url=https://twitter.com/sierralunabot/status/1447494127243853828]Patrick Kenneth Langner[/url] for Rutherford's voice! ːrutherfordwː

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9849113/3d17580ca17ca96d24e34267bdd471dd01d41101.png[/img]

Now that the main characters have their respective voice actors, that's one less thing to worry about! ːclaineohohoː Thanks to the voice actors who auditioned for the role, rest assured we'll have more in the near future!

As for the game itself - we're still in the process of improving visuals and special effects. This time Tobby (aka gtdcarthage, our background artist) will personally oversee the process from ship artwork to weapon particle effects, so expect screenshots/gifs in the coming updates! ːashtonglareː

To make the process straightforward, we'll have a test stage which will serve as the foundation of arcade mode (basically it cycles between development screen and stage battles, then autosaving progress), so hopefully that hits two birds with one stone! ːjeanthinkː

Fun fact for people new to Sierra Ops, we originally had side-view ship visuals.  That kinda spiraled out of control due to our inexperience in programming at the time, as we knew little about optimization so the game became slower and slower. We even switched to 3d to not make the models look too flat, but that limited the number of ships displayed on-screen further. Eventually, we decided to knife it and just simplify to top-down view which honestly gave us lots of room for customizations. ːtiredadmiralː

Last but not the least, as for episode 3 progress - we're working on an animated sequence for one of episode 3's important scenes. It's gonna take a bit to complete but here's a WIP so far: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9849113/7a4381200c0a77debabffd5a01fb7d7dc3b8bcb9.gif[/img]

Youko will finish writing the intro for the second game within the week, this will help me and Tobby decide which CGs and mechs to be produced. The new artworks will also be shown in the coming updates, please look forward to it!

Thank you for supporting the game as always.ːaiheartː

notes.title: Weekly Update #12 - The Narrative Development Process
notes.notes:
Heyo, it's Youko and time for the weekly update. Since the majority of last week was dedicated to planning, it's a bit hard to explain without a few spoilers. We really want the beginning of the second game to be impactful so we're taking time to really think about it properly. Let's just say that there's lots of action and intrigue ahead, so look forward to that! Since we've been thinking so much about planning the game out at large, we thought it would be a good time to talk about our development process! 

[b]Before that, let's quickly go over last week's notable updates!:[/b]

1. Thank you to everyone who applied to our casting call! We'll get back to you as soon as possible as we go through each submission properly! There are currently 100+ submissions again so, uh, we'll do our best to finish going over everyone's auditions asap... ːtiredadmiralː We're also considering potentially voicing Arne, Dermot and Floris (the other CIC officers), but that's up in the air at the moment. ːjeanthinkː

2. We've been massively revamping the voiced-line playback system so implementing voices is easier and no mishaps happen (lol wouldn't it be awkward if someone came back from the grave to tell you that you did a good job in battle???)

3. We will be releasing Sierra Ops 2 in early access with arcade mode and story mode available from the beginning. Hopefully, this will be enough to balance the needs of all our players! Arcade mode in particular will feature a lot more parts, upgrades, and arsenal than in story and normal. The programmers are working hard to get the balance right on this and give you the combat freedom plus challenge you crave (if that's your thing). 

4. Anddd your weekly AU Junius update!
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9849113/616a03bd98ba2ad63690d5ab99a631b75675c724.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9849113/ff340989d6dd5acf13ce2b495b03cf13ade2f35f.png[/img][/url]
[i](Click to enlarge)[/i]

[h3]Now, onto the main topic of the day, the narrative development process:[/h3]

When we started working on the modern iteration of Sierra, we had several key points we had in mind for where the story and gameplay would end up and where things started. The question was how to actually get all the way to the end. ːjeanthinkː

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9849113/b3b437ae9ab1d38daad4700c9964341dbe52d9de.jpg[/img]

Sierra is a complex game in both its narrative and gameplay mechanics. We aim to give players a sense of choice by making sure the world reflects your actions in a way that both makes sense and is engaging. That often means trying to consider what possibilities exist and how far we could realistically let them extend before things got unreasonable. ːallenshockː

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9849113/a799a560adb5290c7c599da1abc9ab4a646e2b5f.jpg[/img]

If you're a fan of the Mass Effect series, you understand this struggle all too well. You want to give your players freedom, but you have to prioritise the best experience for most people with the limited amount of time and budget you have. Bioware decided to largely contain the impact of choices to its specific story beat/ mission. We've attempted to emulate that approach with the way we've structured our side missions, but the same can't be said for the main missions. ːtiredadmiralː

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9849113/558076f61fcbcab0e7cc18d1cf388248b35ae0b0.jpg[/img]

Unlike Mass Effect, we focus on dynamic and fluid character relationships that are both impacted by your direct actions and that specific moment in time instead of the more instance-based design of other games. As a result, we've had to consider all the possible range of reactions from each person for each moment in pretty much any combination you can think of. The end result is the script exponentially expanding no matter how much we try to streamline branches into something manageable. ːashtonglareː You can almost think of it like being the dungeon master of a role playing game, only instead of reacting to player choice in real time, you have to write every possibility out instead. Sadly, we don't have infinite amounts of time to flesh out every minor possibility, so we've settled on a few guiding principles to the narrative design:

1. If it's a major plot point that can potentially change the plot or story progression in a very major way, we will funnel players into making an informed choice as much as possible without being too rail-roady before we decisively split the branches. 

2. If it doesn't fit the above, it's still possible to get to the end of the game as long as you try hard enough during battles, even if the end result isn't what's considered "ideal". 

3. All "bad" results or endings will have some merit in terms of information revealed or narrative purpose, even if it may just be teasing at further events we are unable to make with the scope of the project. 

We'll have to see how effective all these measures are, but we hope it's something you can be excited about! 

That's the end of our brief development process blog for today! Thanks for supporting the game! ːaiheartː

notes.title: Weekly Update #11 - Rutherford Voice Acting Call!
notes.notes:
Heyo, it's Youko and this week's update is more on the state of affairs rather than game progress. ːjeanthinkː

That said, we have made more progress on the game in the form of more art and gameplay stages. We're working on adding more interesting allied and enemy ships to the game to make the battles more enjoyable so look forward to that. ːclaineohohoː Tobby has been making new fancy backgrounds for chapter 4, while Tooaya has also been non-stop working on AU Junius art - she's almost done with everything! ːashtonglareː

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9849113/1381fa800aa719f8e7705c29e2ec240f96297e34.png[/img]

Now, onto the actual topics of discussion, two weeks ago we said we'd be posting a casting call for Rutherford. Considering he is a crew member you meet often and he plays an important role as the lead engineer for Sierra, it's important he has a presence in the game and his number of lines reflects that. After some careful consideration, we decided to scale back voice acting to gameplay only for now as it would seem strange for certain characters to be voiced while others are not. 

[b][url=https://twitter.com/sierralunabot/status/1440502354621566994]Here's our voice acting call post on Twitter![/url][/b]

Please look forward to the upcoming patch for Sierra Ops!
- Gameplay voices (voice can be turned off via slider in game settings)
- WASD as default keys for battle camera scrolling.

This week we have some important things to announce!

First, we'd like to thank everyone for 100+ reviews! ːaiheartː

Even though only 11 reviews actually count towards our general review count below the top-right banner and in search results due to the way Steam counts reviews (they only count reviews from people who directly paid for the game to prevent review skewing), we're very grateful for the feedback (even if some of them are just complaining there's no translation ːjuniusfglareː ).

Next up on the agenda, we would like to announce that we are officially recruiting for a replacement VA for Rutherford. Sadly, his current VA is too busy with other projects... ːtiredadmiralː We'll be releasing a twitter recruitment call soon, so please look out for that if you'd be interested in working with us! ːashtonglareː

Onto actual game updates, we've been working to improve some UI elements. The most major change is that we've replaced the original roman numeral system weapon groups to color coding and adding the ability to rename them. notes.notes:
Heyo, Youko here and it's time for the weekly update! ːashtonglareː

First things first, we'd like to give massive thanks to [url=https://twitter.com/WhoIsAllenChan]Allen Chan[/url] (CV for Ashton) and [url=https://twitter.com/EliseMeggie]Meggie Elise[/url] (CV for Female Junius) for sending in their VA lines so quickly! We really appreciate the enthusiasm, professionalism, and effort they put into making the game better! ːaiheartː

Moving onto the actual update, this week we'll be trying something new. If you read the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/364210/view/2972925916153481066]last update[/url] or have played the game in the last week, you'll notice that we've added the new mode selection screen. Currently, we're focusing on story mode as soon as possible, but we'd like some feedback on how we should implement it, especially with accessibility in mind! ːjeanthinkː
 
The main two concerns with the mode are:
[olist]
[*]The battles are part of the story, so how should they be depicted?
[*]Should fail or non-perfect battle outcomes be accessible since they are a somewhat significant part of the story? 
[/olist]
We've thrown around a few ideas and our promising ones so far are:

[olist]
[*]Give the player and all allies an immortality toggle and boost the speed of how things play out, making the combat extremely easy and quick to get through, but still require some player input. It'll still impact outcomes that are time-based. There is a potential we can add a toggle to the immortality in the options that allows players to turn it off if they would like to experience the less perfect states. 
[*]Some sort of automated cutscene/scripted battle that concludes very quickly. This option mostly limits the battle end stats to perfect or at least "very good", but will make it so no input is required whatsoever. 
[*]Adding some sort of "surrender" option or choice selection that lets you pick between completion states. This would be the most straightforward and easy to control option, but most of the battle dialogue will be summed up/skipped, which isn't ideal.
[/olist]
We're very open to other suggestions and opinions, especially from the folks looking forward to story mode! Any feedback would be very helpful! ːjeanthinkː

Story mode aside, we've been making progress on Episode 3! Our background artist, Tobby, has been working hard on stages and backgrounds! He's finished up the Chapter 4 Main mission stage and will be working on further backgrounds next to better flesh out the world! ːallenshockː

More work is being done on the side missions as they're rather beefy. I'll be able to elaborate soon, but it's very hard to talk about them without spoilers... ːtiredadmiralː

[i][h3]On the bugfix side of things: [/h3][/i]
We've found a bug in S rank calculation preventing some people from getting the S-rank achievement. A fix will be applied next patch which should be coming very soon! If you were eligible for the achievement, loading the save and getting to the report card screen should automatically give you it.

If you happen to stumble across a bug, please report it to [url=https://discord.gg/TRuCZZXuwc]our discord server[/url] or in this steam post: https://steamcommunity.com/app/364210/discussions/1/3037102935217579854/ along with your zipped up saves. (Instructions in the steam forum post)

Thank you for supporting the game! ːaiheartː

notes.title: Episode 3 Progress Update #5
notes.notes:
[i]Join our [url=https://discord.gg/TRuCZZXuwc]Discord[/url] to get the latest updates![/i]
 
Heyo, it's Youko, and it's time for our monthly update already!

There's a huge announcement looming in the near future but for now let's focus on this week's updates until we have concrete news to share! Let's just say it's about the update schedule and leave it at that. 😅
 
On the writing front, there's not much to say outside of progress on side quests is continuing. 
 We're probably looking at the next two weeks being dedicated to this so I'll be sharing a bit more about our design philosophy in the next few coming weeks. The biggest change right now is that we'll be switching from UK to US English. The reason behind this change is due to the majority of our players being from the US and myself being from Canada. If you didn't know already, Canada uses an odd mix of UK and US English, with the majority of vocabulary leaning US, but spelling leaning UK. After some discussion, US English is the easiest for everyone so we will be officially switching to that. Sorry for any inconvenience they may cause! We may eventually add UK English back in as a language option once localization starts to happen, but things are up in the air for now.
 
Writing aside, things have been moving in the art and gameplay departments! First off, we'll be switching Lapis to a more conventional WASD control scheme where w is up, s is down, etc etc, instead of the directing she's facing in being w and backwards being s. This change is being made due to some feedback we've been given on the [url=https://discord.gg/TRuCZZXuwc]discord server[/url], so please join if you'd like to contribute to discourse and the continued development of the game! This patch will officially go live within next week along with more typo and bug fixes.
 
In the art department, we're starting to work on backgrounds and other visual assets for later missions in the game. As a sneak peek, have a gander at these amazing backdrops our lovely BG Artist whipped up!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9849113/e05c33c94d3215cb498378c3b6f8fde45072c0d1.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/9849113/3c22b005fa9511fc086fe71720768f5b852d01c1.png[/img]

We've also officially casted Ashton McCarthy's voice actor, [url=https://twitter.com/WhoIsAllenChan]Allen Chan[/url]!
 
Thanks to everyone who applied for Ashton's role! Allen did really great in the auditions by being consistent with the character tone all throughout the dialogs. There were entries who did just as great as Allen, we just didn't expect to have 120+ submissions 😅 It all boiled down to whoever did all of Ashton's lines, followed instructions/never going OOC, and showed genuine interest in the project.
 
We know we said we're going to reply to each email but turns out we ended up using most of July to fix bugs and other issues for Episode 2... 😭 But please don't worry! We still have more character roles available in the future and we'll surely let everyone know!
 
Thank you for supporting the game and I'll see you next week!

notes.title: Episode 3 Progress Update #4
notes.notes:
[i]Join our [url=https://discord.gg/TRuCZZXuwc]Discord[/url] to get the latest updates![/i]

Heyo, Youko here!

Sorry for the absence last week!😅 I was super sick from getting my second vaccine shot and it took pretty much all weekend plus the start of the week to recover.

This week officially marks the start of side missions (for me at least). While the guys are working on yet more obscure bugs, I've been preparing the finer materials so work through side missions progresses smoothly! 

Right now we're looking at possibly 8 optional missions for the first free roam period of episode 3. Sierra Ops was designed as a multi-playthrough game so it's impossible to see all the missions in one run so be sure to have your saves ready or hunker down and wait for NG+ release so you can reap those NG+ bonuses (and extra content). Generally we try to have at least three new side quests per free roam, but this one is extra stuffed.

The free roam leading into chapter 4 will be the first time we introduce chain missions! Chain missions are missions that are only available if prior requirements are met. Usually this means completing an optional mission or getting a specific result during another part of the game. You can almost consider these hidden missions if you'd like since some of them are quite difficult to unlock. While they're generally not mandatory, you will want to see them if you want the best outcome possible or just to experience all the content. This also means that missions will now start featuring more dynamic elements where succeeding one step may mean another is far easier (or harder) than it could have been. These sorts of missions are quite difficult to design, balance, and write for so we hope you look forward to them. 

There's not much I can reveal with spoilers, but expect a few tougher decisions coming your way. 

Writing aside, we’ve started working on a few other exoframes that will appear in the game! The modeling for one of the new Ares frames is done with animation rigging being planned for this week. (Maybe even a sneak preview...?)

Lapis has also seen some more love with work being put into implementing its new development screen. We don’t have an actual screenshot to show yet, but expect a proper introduction in the monthly big update next week! 

If you want to help support us, please leave a review (or update your existing one) here on Steam! We’re working hard to bring you new content as soon as possible!

Thank you for supporting the game 🥰

notes.title: Episode 3 Progress Update #1
notes.notes:
(Reposted from our Discord server : https://discord.gg/TRuCZZXuwc )

Heyyyo, Youko here!

It's officially Friday in some parts of the world so here's your first weekly update on episode 3 WIP. (:discord emote:)

[h2]Here’s a rough outline of how these are going to work:[/h2]

Basically once a week (usually on Friday) me or another member of the team is going to discuss some of the work we’ve completed this week similar to how a Patreon would operate. A larger update with some visuals will be roughly posted around once a month. This ranges from WIP work to some sneak previews so stay tuned for that. 

Feel free to discuss these updates in spoilers or the lounge. I’ll usually be around when these drop to answer any questions if there are any. 

That said, since Sierra Ops is such a large game for our tiny team, we all heavily specialize on our own respective fields so expect a very heavy story/ writing focus from me, general behind the scenes from Jason, and gameplay stuff from Glean. 

We really want to try to be more transparent about what is going on with development after how much episode 2 was delayed. Hopefully, this will help ease some anxiety about the state of the game and prevent more “abandonware” claims. (:sweating cat:)

[h2]Anyway, here is the actual update:[/h2]

I’m happy to announce that we are officially starting to transition from bug-fixes and polishing to work on episode 3!

For any of you who weren’t aware, Sierra Ops has been in development hell for a long, long time. The original first draft of the script was completed in some time 2019. Since then, a lot of things about the game has changed. From the inclusion of more concrete world building to exoframes, the script has seen some massive edits from that first draft to release in both episode 1 and 2. In fact, the entirety of Episode 2’s script was originally only around 40k~ and ended up ballooning past 120k. A lot of this old material was particularly rough so it needed a lot of reworking to be usable, but I hope you’re happy with the result. 

Now, the question is “does this also apply to episode 3”? 

Right now it’s a tentative half-yes, half-no. After taking another look at the existing writing, it’s a lot more workable than episode 2 so the amount of rewriting I have to do is substantially decreased. That doesn’t mean it’s going to be quick process, but it is a lot better of a situation than Episode 2’s script.

Currently, we’re planning to work in a chronological fashion to minimize late-development edits and changes. Hopefully, this will speed things up and improve our QA process. A lot of new content will need to be incorporated so expect the writing process to be an ongoing effort while we attempt to coordinate our individual workloads better to deliver the game faster.

Believe me, none of us want the next episode to take another 1.5 years to release. We are doing everything we can to shrink that timespan.

[h2]Now that the context has been taken care of, here is the actual writing progress this week:[/h2]

Jason and I have more or less finalized the mission list and outline for the free roam period of Chapter 3 and have completely planned out Chapter 4. 

Chapter 3 free roam features the most missions yet with the appearance of our first chain mission – a mission that is only available if certain outcome in a pervious mission was achieved. Judging by the steam achievements, it’s something many of you will enjoy. 

Following the actions-reactions trend, we’re planning to feature more optional missions that take into account your performance and actions in earlier side quests or main story missions now that Junius is starting to find his feet and is actually making an impact on the war. Specific battles may become significantly easier to harder depending on prior actions. Heck, some outcomes are locked unless certain actions are taken earlier so plan accordingly. We highly recommend keeping different save states so you can explore all the possible outcomes in a situation!

Moving on from Chapter 3 for a moment, Chapter 4 will mark a big change aboard Sierra. If you can guess what it is, you get full points (not that it’s particularly difficult). I’ll update you guys with more information once we’re actually closer to working on the mission itself. Let’s just say it’s another double-trouble mission. 

As for what physical writing has been completed this week, I’ve been working on bridging the end of Episode 2 into Episode 3. First up is the break that Junius originally attempted to call at the end of Episode 2 only to be interrupted and called to other duties. Only about 1/3 of the breaks have been edited or rewritten, so I’ll be continuing that next week. 

That’s it for this week. Next update coming next Friday!

Thanks for supporting the game! ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Sierra Ops Episode 2 Update, and Original Soundtrack Volume 1 released!

Hello everyone,

From our previous update, we were thinking about doing public beta testing. However we've decided against it in favor of adding and refining content in the game to give a more complete experience. While episode one had many issues that were only resolved two months into release, episode two is in a far more stable state.

We also want to say [b]thank you[/b] because we've reached more than 10,000 downloads! Our best buddy Rutherford here sincerely appreciate your support :)
